investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-26T04:40–04:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient peer-pod VM quota and 4 nodes failing node affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state and times out before the eval runner can observe a VM ID or a running/idle/ready remote state. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner bug. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — existing peer-pod VMs are occupying all available slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the 4 non-peer-pod nodes may have had their labels changed or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity rules no longer match any available node, reducing the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and then to 0 after quota exhaustion.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up — the eval runner uses withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) but if a prior run was interrupted, orphaned VMs may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.
[Possible] Cluster node count reduction — if one or both peer-pod-capable nodes became NotReady or were drained, the effective quota would drop to zero even if per-node limits are unchanged.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that are eligible by affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod times out (~142–146 s), causing the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) to fail before any state polling can occur. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes and affinity mismatch on the other 4, leaving zero viable placement targets. This directly explains the pod-stuck-unscheduled message and the complete absence of evidence.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is already constrained to 2 nodes. If affinity rules changed or node labels drifted, the effective capacity could have dropped to zero even with some vm slots remaining.

TERTIARY — Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if other pods (eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods from prior stuck runs) are holding vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, new pods cannot be placed until those slots are released.

QUATERNARY — Eval runner does not skip or short-circuit when a prior sibling (remote-agent-create) already reported an Unschedulable failure: remote-agent-create ended at 04:43:09 and remote-agent-state started at 04:43:09, suggesting the state eval may have attempted a fresh createAgent call into the same saturated cluster rather than reusing or skipping.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-26T04:40–04:48Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the 6-node production cluster has zero schedulable capacity for kata.peerpods.io/vm pods, with 2 nodes reporting insufficient peer-pod VM quota and 4 nodes failing node affinity/selector matching. Because the agent pod never scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or remote state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. As a result, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state and times out before the eval runner can observe a VM ID or a running/idle/ready remote state. This is an infrastructure-layer capacity or configuration constraint, not an eval runner bug. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState was ever written, confirming the pod never reached a schedulable state.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error message, latencyMs=154955, evidenceKeys=[] — third independent run confirms the condition is persistent across the eval window, not a transient blip.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1880-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) which must schedule a kata peer-pod; if that pod never becomes ready, no evidence is written and the check fails.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource quota is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — existing peer-pod VMs are occupying all available slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.

[Likely] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift — the 4 non-peer-pod nodes may have had their labels changed or the pod spec's nodeSelector/affinity rules no longer match any available node, reducing the schedulable pool from 6 to 2 nodes and then to 0 after quota exhaustion.

[Possible] Leaked or zombie remote-agent VMs from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up — the eval runner uses withCleanup (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) but if a prior run was interrupted, orphaned VMs may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots.
[Possible] Cluster node count reduction — if one or both peer-pod-capable nodes became NotReady or were drained, the effective quota would drop to zero even if per-node limits are unchanged.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that are eligible by affinity/selector. With 0/6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every attempt to schedule a remote agent pod times out (~142–146 s), causing the eval runner's createAgent step (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) to fail before any state polling can occur. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 nodes and affinity mismatch on the other 4, leaving zero viable placement targets. This directly explains the pod-stuck-unscheduled message and the complete absence of evidence.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning the schedulable pool is already constrained to 2 nodes. If affinity rules changed or node labels drifted, the effective capacity could have dropped to zero even with some vm slots remaining.

TERTIARY — Concurrent remote agent workloads consuming all available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if other pods (eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods from prior stuck runs) are holding vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes, new pods cannot be placed until those slots are released.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 04:43 and 04:48 UTC on 2026-06-26 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: 0/6 nodes are available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. Because the remote agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~142–146 s), preventing the eval from reaching the runtime stage and producing any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 146s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-create: identical scheduling error message, latencyMs=153981, endedAt=2026-06-26T04:43:09.004Z — the earliest failing check in the sequence, confirming the condition predates the runtime check.
sibling.remote-agent-state: same scheduling error (pod stuck unscheduled for 142s), latencyMs=149226, endedAt=2026-06-26T04:45:38.231Z — all three checks share the same infrastructure failure mode.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=154955, status=fail — the probe ran for ~155 s, consistent with waiting for the pod scheduling timeout before giving up.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence keys were collected, confirming the agent process never started and the runtime response was never reached.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, consistent with the agent pod never being scheduled.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1917-1918: the runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) immediately after acquiring orgId — pod scheduling is the first infrastructure gate; failure here prevents all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:183-185: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are marked required=true; remote-agent-runtime is required=false — all three failed, indicating the shared pod scheduling layer is the common failure point.
possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods. Preemption found no victims, meaning no lower-priority pods are present to evict.

[High confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are at capacity. A cluster topology change (node removal, label change, or taint addition) could have reduced the eligible node pool.

[Medium confidence] Cluster under-provisioning or node failure: one or more of the kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may have been drained, cordoned, or lost, reducing available VM capacity below the demand level at the time of the eval run.

reproductionSteps.label: Run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow. Expect the same Unschedulable error if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is still exhausted.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: All three checks should reproduce the same pod stuck unscheduled message if the root cause is cluster-wide capacity exhaustion.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Use kubectl or the cluster's node resource API to check the allocatable and requested quantities of kata.peerpods.io/vm on the nodes that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm on the eligible nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Identify which workloads hold the VM slots and whether any are in a stuck, dead, or unresponsive state that could be freed.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for pending or stuck remote-agent pods in the cluster namespace
reproductionSteps.details: Look for pods in Pending state with the Unschedulable condition to confirm the scheduling backlog and its age.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm)
affectedAreas.reason: All three remote-agents checks fail at pod scheduling before any agent process starts. The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted on the 2 nodes eligible by node affinity/selector, blocking all remote agent creation in production-api.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch at line 1913–1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which triggers pod scheduling. Scheduling failure prevents evidence collection and causes the expected-output contract to be entirely unmet.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create eval check (sibling, required=true)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check remote-agent-create (required=true, line 183) failed with the identical scheduling message, confirming the capacity problem affects agent creation as well as runtime.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-state eval check (sibling, required=true)
affectedAreas.reason: Sibling check remote-agent-state (required=true, line 184) also failed with the same scheduling error, indicating state polling is blocked by the same pod scheduling failure.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — degraded/outage threshold
affectedAreas.reason: Feature is configured with degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (lines 187–188). With all three checks failing, the feature is at or past the outage threshold in the eval system.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately check the current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes to determine whether the exhaustion is ongoing.
Identify and audit all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots — particularly any that are stuck, dead, or in a terminal state — and free slots occupied by non-running workloads.

If capacity is genuinely exhausted by live workloads, evaluate whether additional kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes need to be added to the cluster or whether the VM slot quota per node can be increased.
Investigate whether the 4 nodes that do not match the pod's node affinity/selector could be made eligible (e.g., by adding the required label), to expand the schedulable pool.

Once cluster capacity is restored, re-run all three remote-agents eval checks to confirm recovery and that all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are collected and the message assertion ('hello from aura') passes.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run remote-agent-runtime eval to confirm persistence of scheduling failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion is ongoing or was transient at the time of the original run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks together
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the shared scheduling failure persists across all three checks and whether the feature remains at outage threshold.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity and allocations
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly proves or disproves the capacity exhaustion hypothesis and identifies which workloads hold the VM slots.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Query the Kubernetes API for allocatable and used kata.peerpods.io/vm quantities on all 6 nodes, filtered to the 2 that match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List Pending remote-agent pods and their scheduling events
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms the scheduling backlog is real and shows how many pods are queued, helping estimate the severity of the capacity shortfall.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Retrieve pods in Pending state with the Unschedulable condition in the remote-agents namespace and inspect their events for the exact scheduling failure message.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Review cluster node events around 04:40–04:48 UTC on 2026-06-26
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Would distinguish between sustained capacity exhaustion and a node-loss event that suddenly reduced available VM slots.
recommendedVerifierProbes.details: Check for node drain, cordon, NotReady, or resource pressure events on the kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in the window preceding the first failing check (remote-agent-create, endedAt 04:43:09).

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful remote-agent pod scheduling event on the same cluster at the same time would disprove that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was fully exhausted.
kubectl output showing available (unallocated) kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes at the time of the eval run would disprove the capacity exhaustion hypothesis.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime immediately after the failure window, without any cluster changes, would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the 4 non-affinity nodes were recently relabeled or that the pod spec's node selector was recently tightened would shift the cause from capacity exhaustion to a topology/configuration change.
Cluster event logs showing a node drain or failure on one of the 2 eligible nodes just before 04:43 UTC would support the node-loss hypothesis over pure capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes and fails with a warning before full exhaustion is reached.

Add a cluster node affinity health check that verifies the expected number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's node selector are in Ready state, alerting if the eligible node pool drops below a minimum threshold.

Add a Pending pod age check that fires if any remote-agent pod remains in Pending/Unschedulable state for more than a configurable threshold (e.g., 60 s), catching scheduling pressure before it causes full eval timeouts.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that tracks the delta between kata.peerpods.io/vm slots allocated and the count of running remote-agent pods, alerting if slots are held without corresponding running pods (indicating leaked or stuck allocations).
